sentences.text:
[LA.App. Nos.109/2023, 263/2021, 240/2021, 253/2021, 42/2023, 43/2023, 27/2023, 39/2023,
37/2023, 44/2023] Amit Rawal, J.
1. Present appeals have arisen out of the common judgment dated 10.03.2016 and 24.02.2016 of the Reference Court in the following LARs:
LAR Nos.161 of 2014, 185 of 2014, 228 of 2014, 377 of 2014, 186 of 2014, 349 of 2014,
169 of 2014, 187 of 2014, 170 of 2014 and 171 of 2014.

2. Succinctly the facts in brief are that the Government of Kerala caused a notification under Section 4 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act on 25.10.2007 for acquiring the land of 0.1567 hectors for providing approach road to the bridge situated in Kunnamagalam Village now Municipal Corporation, District Kozhikode.
The aforementioned acquisition proceedings remained under stay 2024:KER:76710 LA.APP.NO.109/2023 & Conn. Cases on being challenged by various land owners from 2008-2009.

The award was pronounced on 29.12.2012 whereby the Land Acquisition Officer relying upon the basic document of 2005 assessed compensation as Rs.36,250/- (Rupees thirty six thousand two fifty only) per Are.

All the land owners sought reference under Section 18, in reference Sugathan C vs Special Tahsildar (La) on 9 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/20740795/
12 numbers as noticed above.
Appellants have not examined any witnesses or brought on record any evidence.
3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellants submitted that during the pendency of the appeals I.A.No.1361/2016 and I.A.No.1394/2016 were filed for placing on record additional documents.
First application was dismissed, however, the second application was disposed of vide order dated 24.02.2016 by granting two(2) weeks time, but did not avail that also.

The aforementioned opportunity was not availed leading to submission of another application I.A.No.1395/2016 for direction to the Sub Registrar Office, 2024:KER:76710 LA.APP.NO.109/2023 & Conn. Cases Chathamangalam to produce the register which was dismissed by the Reference Court on 29.02.2016.

Instead of challenging the aforementioned order in accordance with law,
another I.A.No.1495/2016 was preferred to re-open the cases and grant three(3) weeks' time to tender the evidence, which was also dismissed vide order dated 01.03.2016.

It was further contended that the appellants have been granted only Rs.40,000/- (Rupees forty thousand only) per cent against the claim of Rs.10 lakhs per cent, being valuable piece of land it can openly fetch a higher price than the one assessed for grant of compensation by the Land Acquisition Officer and the Reference Court, being only 200-250 meters away from the National Highway (N.H 212).
4.

On the other hand, Sri.T.K.Shajahan, learned Government Pleader representing the State submits that the appellants have miserably failed to place on record the evidence and rightly so, the reference court did not 2024:KER:76710 LA.APP.NO.109/2023 & Conn. Cases enhance the amount of compensation, but by relying upon some findings in the other references, awarded the compensation of Rs.1,96,900/- (Rupees one lakh ninety six thousand nine hundred only) per Are along with other statutory benefits.

He relied upon the decision of this Court dated 10.07.2019 in Land Acquisition Appeal No.23/2015 in respect of acquisition which is close-by to the land in dispute whereby the compensation has been enhanced to Rs.75,000/- (Rupees seventy five thousand only) per cent.
5.

We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and appraised the paper books and of the view that the orders referred to above declining the application were also appealable along with appeal filed under Section 54 of the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act by invoking the provisions of Order XLIII Rule 1A of the Code of Civil Procedure.

Even if those orders have not been challenged, appeals could have been accompanied by an application under Order XLI Rule 27 2024:KER:76710 LA.APP.NO.109/2023 & Conn. Cases by placing on record the sale deed of the area close-by to the land in question and the date of acquisition ie., October, 2007, for determination of just and equitable compensation.
6.

It is settled law that on account of lack of legal advice or any other lapse, the litigants cannot be made to suffer for the reason that the valuable piece of land has been acquired and have not been compensating in terms of money as per the market value of land.
We drew our aforementioned observation from the ratio decidendi culled out by the Supreme Court in Rafiq & Another vs Munshilal & Another (AIR 1981 SC 1400).

We are of the view that it would be in the fitness of things that the matter at the level of the Reference Court is required to be revisited by affording four(4) effective opportunities each to the land owners as well as the State to produce or counter the evidence for the purpose of seeking the enhancement of compensation by relying upon the 2024:KER:76710 LA.APP.NO.109/2023 & Conn.
Cases documents which may be necessary for adjudication of lis in accordance with law.
Accordingly, the order of the Reference Court is set aside.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The award was pronounced on 29.12.2012 whereby the Land Acquisition Officer relying upon the basic document of 2005 assessed compensation as Rs.36,250/- (Rupees thirty six thousand two fifty only) per Are.
Appellants have not examined any witnesses or brought on record any evidence.
Instead of challenging the aforementioned order in accordance with law,
another I.A.No.1495/2016 was preferred to re-open the cases and grant three(3) weeks' time to tender the evidence, which was also dismissed vide order dated 01.03.2016.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Even if those orders have not been challenged, appeals could have been accompanied by an application under Order XLI Rule 27 2024:KER:76710 LA.APP.NO.109/2023 & Conn. Cases by placing on record the sale deed of the area close-by to the land in question and the date of acquisition ie., October, 2007, for determination of just and equitable compensation.
6.
It is settled law that on account of lack of legal advice or any other lapse, the litigants cannot be made to suffer for the reason that the valuable piece of land has been acquired and have not been compensating in terms of money as per the market value of land.
We drew our aforementioned observation from the ratio decidendi culled out by the Supreme Court in Rafiq & Another vs Munshilal & Another (AIR 1981 SC 1400).
We are of the view that it would be in the fitness of things that the matter at the level of the Reference Court is required to be revisited by affording four(4) effective opportunities each to the land owners as well as the State to produce or counter the evidence for the purpose of seeking the enhancement of compensation by relying upon the 2024:KER:76710 LA.APP.NO.109/2023 & Conn.
Cases documents which may be necessary for adjudication of lis in accordance with law.
